subject.title: fix: gateway-owned work fails through same-host relay

question: Should Gateway-owned recovery and native approvals permanently use lifecycle-bound in-process principals instead of authenticating a self-client through the Gateway WebSocket boundary?
rationale: Both designs can fix the topology bug, but choosing the permanent internal-authority model determines whether Gateway-owned work bypasses network authentication by design and therefore requires explicit owner intent.

options.title: Approve closed in-process principals
options.body: Accept the branch's topology-independent model with immutable narrow method sets, instance lifecycle ownership, and continued denial of external host-interface authority.

options.title: Require an authenticated self-client
options.body: Keep internal work on the WebSocket path and provide a device-authenticated or otherwise explicit service identity that survives same-host relay topology.

options.title: Extend same-host equivalence
options.body: Treat verified local interface addresses as loopback-equivalent, accepting a broader network-auth trust predicate instead of introducing internal principals.

recommendation.title: Approve closed in-process principals
recommendation.body: Accept the branch's topology-independent model with immutable narrow method sets, instance lifecycle ownership, and continued denial of external host-interface authority.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is explicitly associated with Gateway, Security, and Agents ownership and has prior merged Gateway scope-contract work.
